title: iif() bare catch turns a broken condition into 'always take the then-branch'
existing_state: Iif evaluates its condition with ExpressionEvaluator inside a bare `catch` (Services/Scripting/Functions/MathFunctions.cs:184-193): when evaluation throws — e.g. `iif(lenght(x) > 0, "up", "down")` where the unknown function makes ExpressionParser throw FormatException (ExpressionParser.cs:436) — the fallback re-resolves the ENTIRE condition string as a plain value via JsonUtilities.ResolveJsonValue (MathFunctions.cs:191). That resolution falls through to the literal string "lenght(x) > 0" (per the fall-through at JsonUtilities.cs:312-333), which is non-empty and therefore truthy, so the then-branch is taken unconditionally. Any typo or evaluator error inside an iif condition thus silently pins the result to the true-value on every host, every run.
recommendation: Narrow the fallback in MathFunctions.Iif: only fall back to truthiness when the condition contains no comparison/logical operators (the legitimate 'simple value' case the comment describes); let FormatException from the evaluator propagate so the step fails with 'Unknown function: lenght'. This also becomes moot for the typo case if the unknown-function fall-through (BUG-010) is fixed.
user_benefit: iif is the branching primitive people embed in set:/send: lines; today a typo flips it into a constant. Propagating the parse error makes the failure visible at the exact step instead of producing confidently wrong branch decisions fleet-wide.

evidence.note: bare catch at 188-193 re-resolves the condition as a value; literal string is truthy
fallback path resolves the condition text to itself as a string
